The existing failing test first compares every current definition to the pre-reference frozen fixture, so that assertion is stale. Separately, static source analysis proves the submitted-task resolver rejects the exact old atomic material version before it can return the old parser; that recovery compatibility gap is real but was not directly reached by the supplied failing test.

findings.minimum_outcome: Replace the obsolete all-current-equals-old assertion with two explicit contracts: today material definition includes the authorized reference field and has its own derived version; old frozen definitions/JSON/version/schema remain byte-unchanged and are independently restorable.

authorization_basis.meaning: The accepted product contract explicitly requires reference image generation and first-frame video through the shared asset.generate chain, with owner validation and frozen file identity. Reverting current description/schema/version to the old fixture would regress authorized behavior.

exact_write_set_recommendation.why_one_source_is_sufficient: The parent snapshot already stores the complete frozen definition. The resolver is the sole conversion point from that definition to a production-order parser. It can hold a small generic immutable compatibility registry of complete definition + historical schema/parser pairs and try exact complete-definition equality after the current exact match fails. No execution host, DB service, schema, SDK, IPC, or lifecycle change is needed.
implementation_boundary: Current path: rebuild today definition and accept only complete equality, returning today parser.

Legacy path: compare canonical/deep equality against complete immutable historical definitions, then return the paired historical production-order parser and schema. The registry entry may contain the historical material definition as data; control flow must not branch on tool name.
Unknown version, changed description/schema/effect/execution, extra tool, or foreign definition remains rejected.

Keep submitted-task-preparation.service.ts checks unchanged: parent owner/workspace, original call ID/digest, attempt ID, settled receipt, exact schema equality, binding validation, task ID/result kind, and deadlines.
Do not recompute or overwrite the historical digest and do not accept today referenceAssetId under the old version.

required_tests: Old frozen JSON and old material version/schema remain unchanged and resolve to a parser that accepts the old legal object and rejects referenceAssetId/additional properties.
Today material definition still contains referenceAssetId, has the new version, and its parser accepts only the new legal contract.
Mutate each of name/version/description/parameters/effect/execution on an old entry: every mutation rejects. Include unknown/extra tool rejection.
The existing full submitted-task recovery regression keeps the original inputDigest and task ID, preserves owner/workspace and receipt validation, and does not create a second task/call.
Run the originally failing seven-case canvas host file plus the submitted-task recovery file. Do not delete the old fixture or update its JSON/hash to current bytes.
